# E0308: inherent method hides a trait method

A method's name means one member of a type, so an inherent method and a trait's method can't share it. Rename the inherent method.

- Rule: [`traits.name-clashes`](../../reference/11-traits.md#traits.name-clashes)
- Reported at: the trait impl's `impl` keyword, or the inherent method's name when the impl is structural.
- Tier: `core`, checked in the `items` phase

## Example

This program makes the mistake:

```stilt E0308:7
type Point = { x: i64, y: i64 }

impl Point {
  fn show(self) -> str { "({self.x}, {self.y})" }
}

impl Show for Point {
  fn show(self) -> str { "Point({self.x}, {self.y})" }
}
```

This one is fixed:

```stilt
type Point = { x: i64, y: i64 }

impl Point {
  fn pair(self) -> str { "({self.x}, {self.y})" }
}

impl Show for Point {
  fn show(self) -> str { "Point({self.x}, {self.y})" }
}
```
